terra.problem: The gnat joke makes light of the suffering in the warning about sword, famine and plague.
The cookie-dough comparison has no clear connection to guesses jumping ahead of the text.
Referring to the 'second stop' talks about the lesson's structure rather than the passage.
Saying he won't joke comments on how he is telling the passage.
The claim that Nebuchadnezzar carried the exiles to Babylon needs a reference outside this passage.
The text says Shemaiah sent the letters in his own name, but does not say the LORD did not send the letters.

Sending letters in his own name does not establish that Shemaiah signed them or that no king's name appeared on them. The distinction between King Zedekiah and the other Zedekiah also needs support from outside the passage.
The statement that Jeremiah wrote the letter to the exiles needs a reference outside this passage.
Planting a garden does not necessarily mean someone plans to stay and see it grow. The absolute claim that nobody plants one for a short stay is not true.
Saying that not being sent is the whole problem omits that Shemaiah made the exiles trust in a lie and preached rebellion.
The LORD says Shemaiah made the exiles trust in a lie, not merely that they were being led toward it.
The passage also gives Shemaiah's prophesying without being sent and making the exiles trust in a lie as reasons for his punishment.
The passage does add more: Shemaiah prophesied without being sent and made the exiles trust in a lie.
